source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source.authors: Diggs, G. M. Jr.; Lipscomb, B. L.; O'Kennon, R. J.
historical_synonyms_documented: Arbutus xalapensis var. texana (Buckley) A. Gray

morphology_documented.habit: Small evergreen tree or rarely arborescent shrub, 4–6(–10 or more) m tall
morphology_documented.bark: Pinkish to brick red, peeling off in large smooth flakes, exposing distinctive bare branches
morphology_documented.leaves: Alternate, evergreen, leathery, ovate to oval or oblong-elliptic, to 10 cm long × 45 mm wide; entire to serrate; glabrate with age
morphology_documented.flowers: Panicles, perfect flowers, 5 pinkish-white calyx lobes; urn-shaped white or pink-tinged corolla ca. 7 mm; 10 included stamens, 1.5 mm anthers with paired reflexed spurs, opening through terminal pores
morphology_documented.fruit: Roughened/tuberculate spherical fleshy berry 7.5–9 mm diameter, red to yellowish-red
morphology_documented.habitat: Rocky wooded hills, slopes, canyons and plains

source_scope_note: Species vs genus/key-level characters distinguished in text; no undocumented characters inferred.
unresolved_taxonomy_or_source_notes: Historical A. texana and var. texana subsumed under A. xalapensis by flora following Sørensen 1995
Flora cites a small number of Travis County observations; not BONAP county verification
preservation: Additive research record, existing species cards, original media, credits and galleries unchanged
